proof_skeleton_nl: Fix an arbitrary positive integer n, an integer j with 0 <= j <= n - 1, and a real x with j/n <= x < (j + 1)/n. Define t = n*x - j. By L2 and L3, t lies in [0,1), x = T_{n,j}(t), and this coordinate is unique on the cell. By L5, G_{n,j}(t) <= G_{n,j}(0). By L4, this rewrites to F_n(x) <= F_n(j/n). Since the chosen n, j, and x were arbitrary under the stated hypotheses, universal generalization gives exactly the theorem statement.

steps.derives: From the hypotheses j/n <= x < (j + 1)/n and t = n*x - j, obtain 0 <= t < 1, x = T_{n,j}(t), and the uniqueness of this affine coordinate on the cell I_{n,j}.
steps.trivial_justification: This combines direct arithmetic with the cell-parameter uniqueness statement, so it is more than a single inference.

steps.derives: For the specific t from A1, conclude G_{n,j}(t) <= G_{n,j}(0).
steps.trivial_justification: This is a direct instantiation of the bottleneck inequality at the chosen parameter t.

steps.derives: Rewrite G_{n,j}(t) as F_n(x) and G_{n,j}(0) as F_n(j/n), yielding F_n(x) <= F_n(j/n).
steps.trivial_justification: This uses the definitional bridge together with x = T_{n,j}(t) from A1 to rewrite both sides.

steps.derives: Since n, j, and x were arbitrary subject to the hypotheses, conclude the universally quantified theorem: for every positive integer n, every integer j with 0 <= j <= n - 1, and every real x with j/n <= x < (j + 1)/n, one has F_n(x) <= F_n(j/n).
steps.trivial_justification: This is universal generalization from the arbitrary fixed variables.
